originals.caption: Manueline cloisters of the Jerónimos Monastery, Lisbon
originals.inspection: 2007 original individually inspected: two-storey cloister with chamfered inner corners, broad lower arches subdivided by three slender shafts, two upper open arches under each broad bay, pierced round/lobed tracery and projecting piers. True open sky and continuous covered galleries; grass/paths and low fountain distinct. Figures/tourists excluded.

originals.inspection: 2017 original individually inspected: pale limestone church, tall square bell tower with ribbed rounded dome/beaded finial and small corner pinnacles; south wall has giant narrow pointed windows and elaborate projecting central portal, pierced roof parapet and buttresses. originals.caption: The Jerónimos Monastery is a prominent landmark in Lisbon, Portugal and one of the most successful achievements of the Manueline style.

originals.caption: Main portal of Jerónimos Monastery, Lisboa, Portugal
originals.inspection: 2015 south portal original individually inspected: two actual dark door leaves under twin arches; broad shallow canopy arch with crossed ribs, dense tiers of sculptural niches/columns, large narrow pointed flanking windows, nautical rope relief, pierced fleur/foliate parapet, projecting buttress pinnacles and tall central statue/cross above. Preserve recognizable tiers/silhouette; no exact faces/inscriptions or copied image pixels.

originals.caption: Claustro
originals.inspection: 2010 full cloister original individually inspected: actual chamfered corner bays, square court/diagonal dry paths, low circular fountain basin and separate grass panels. Lower broad bays have three slender posts and pierced spandrel/tracery; upper bays have paired arches under broad segmental arch. Parapet medallions and twisted conical pinnacles differ from church roof ornament.

originals.caption: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
originals.inspection: 2018 upper cloister original individually inspected: bell-tower dome is broad/ribbed, surrounded by tall corner pinnacles and crenellated/lobed base; nautical beaded finial/cross and clock below. Two slender spired turrets stand between cloister and dormitory; terracotta back church roof visible. Cloister chamfer, plainer rear church upper wall and patterned parapets constrain rear massing.
